critical.problem: Step 04 fine-print sample rewrites a regulatory-cleared INCI list while labelling it as supplied. Authored: "Aqua, Azelaic Acid, Glycerin, Dimethyl Isosorbide, Tocopherol". The cleared record in TASK_SPEC.json (source_record row 7, table lumora_skus.csv, output sku-module-r007) is "Aqua, Azelaic Acid, Dimethyl Isosorbide, Glycerin, Niacinamide, Allantoin, Bisabolol" — Glycerin and Dimethyl Isosorbide are swapped in order, Niacinamide, Allantoin and Bisabolol are dropped, and Tocopherol is added (it is not in this SKU at all). The row's own note says "Regulatory cleared INCI, set as supplied" and the authored rules say "Cleared INCI lines and claims are fixed and cannot be edited", so the object contradicts itself. brand_assets_status confirms: "The regulatory cleared INCI lines and claims are fixed and cannot be edited."

FABRICATED CLEARED CLAIM in the step 01 sample. The sample reads "Magnesium glycinate, and what it is actually for." The approved cleared sentence in the spec is, verbatim, "A studied dose is the amount used in the research, not the amount that fits on a label." (deliverables editorial-wide-excerpt-1 and the 9:16 cutdown both bind it). Neither "Magnesium" nor "glycinate" appears anywhere in TASK_SPEC.json. This is worse than filler: the row's own note says this slot IS "The cleared sentence", the record's own rules say "never reword a cleared claim line" and "Never run a claim the regulatory reviewer has not cleared", and truth_constraints says "Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features...". The authored spec therefore demonstrates, in its own display sample, the exact thing its rules forbid — an uncleared supplement claim for a brand whose entire positioning is regulatory restraint. Replace the sample with the cleared sentence.

The six cleared actives are L-Ascorbic Acid 15%, Niacinamide 10%, Retinaldehyde 0.1%, Palmitoyl Tripeptide-1, Sodium Hyaluronate + Polyglutamic Acid, and Azelaic Acid 10%. Step 02 sample is "Azelaic Acid Serum"; the record name is "Lumora Azelaic Redness Serum". Step 04 allergen sample invents allergens for a cold-case label. Authored: "Contains wheat, milk and mustard seed. The slicer is shared." Inventing allergen text in the row that defines how allergen lines are set is the highest-risk sample in this set.

Steps 02 and 03 samples conflate three different linesheet pieces into one that does not exist. Step 02 sample "THE WAXED CANVAS CHORE COAT" and Step 03 sample "Ten ounce waxed canvas, felled seams, cast pewter hardware." The actual record is Piece Name "Yard Chore Coat", Fabric "Waxed 10 oz cotton" (cotton, not canvas), Make Note "...blanket-stitch buttonholes, cotton-twill pocket bags, seams taped inside" — taped, not felled, and no metal hardware. "Felled seams" and canvas belong to the Fell Overshirt (12 oz cotton canvas, "Triple-needle felled shoulder and side seams"); "cast-pewter" belongs to the Bench Henley's buttons. Step 04 note and rule 5 read "Wholesale and retail prices take Bitter Medium oldstyle figures at 11 pt and appear on the linesheet only" / "Prices are Bitter Medium oldstyle figures at 11 pt and live only on the linesheet". The brief says only "Prices take Bitter Medium oldstyle figures at 11 pt." Drop 'retail' and name the line card, not a linesheet.

The scale contradicts itself on the signature ratio. Step 01 note: "exactly three times the 22 pt address"; prose: "that figure is always exactly three times the address". But step 01 is 54 pt and step 02 is 22 pt — 54 is 2.45x, not 3x (3x would be 66 pt). Either set the display to 66 pt or state the ratio as approximate and drop "exactly".

Internal contradiction between rules and scale/prose on tracking. rules[4] says "The episode label sets in PP Radio Grotesk Medium at 40 px tracked 80; no other step is tracked out." but scale step 04 (Fine print, Inter Regular, 24 px) carries "tracking":"+10 units", and the prose repeats it ("Step 04, fine print, is the disclosure in Inter Regular at 24 px on 34 px leading, tracking +10 units"). +10 units IS tracked out, so the rule forbids a value the system itself specifies twice. Either the rule must be scoped (e.g. no other step is tracked out above +10, or no display step is tracked out) or step 04 must go to 0.
